newsitem.title: UK: Inchcape gains as analysts raise forecasts.
newsitem.headline: Inchcape gains as analysts raise forecasts.

text.p: Shares in Inchcape Plc advanced on Monday, after analysts were prompted to raise current year earnings forecasts following the group's annual results.
The shares were up 10p at 265-1/2p by 1214 GMT, after earlier touching a high of 270p. Last week the shares fell to a 12-month closing low of 242-1/2p.
Inchcape had earlier announced a 12 percent rise in pretax profits excluding exceptional items, at the top end of market expectations.
Andrew Ripper, industry analyst at Merrill Lynch said he expects to raise his current year forecasts by around five percent to 178 million stg, and just over 19 pence earnings per share.
"The key thing from the meeting was positive comments on prospects for growth," Ripper said. "Particularly the motors division."
Profits from the motors division grew by 29 percent in 1996, helped by a strong performance from the group's Toyota franchises.

Elsewhere, strong cash generation was another feature. The sale of Bain Hogg and Testing Services helped Inchcape wipe out debts of nearly 500 million stg, to leave the group with net cash of 39.9 million stg.
Another analyst, who declined to be named, expected to raise his pretax forecast from 166 to 175 million stg for the current year.
